why: A GREEN-LOOKING CORPUS IS CARRYING A RED NOBODY NAMED. cairn/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector_nexus.py::test_the_fire_path_never_reaches_the_tree FAILS today, bare: 'inspector.py imports outside its allowlist: [cairn.base.nest]'. The tooth pins what the verdict path may reach — its allowlist is a literal tuple in the proof, and every prior addition to it (cairn.chart.verdict 2026-07-29, re + cairn.skill_block 2026-08-01, cairn.import_sieve 2026-08-06) arrived WITH a dated justifying comment naming the ticket that admitted it. cairn.base.nest arrived in 047d633 ('the nest berths at the general level, and the gate that proves it is its own first tenant') and the allowlist was never widened, so the module entered the fire path without passing the gate that exists to decide exactly that. THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a build lands, the corpus is reported at 88/87/1 with the one red named as something else entirely (the /design and /idea omission from node_classes/skill.json), and a second red rides along unmentioned — so the next person to reason about what the verdict path may reach reads a tooth that is not actually holding. THE SHAPE WORTH CARRYING: this is not a wrong allowlist, it is an UNMADE DECISION wearing a passing sweep. Admitting cairn.base.nest may well be correct — it is a pure-AST, tree-free primitive, the same class of thing the tooth's own comments admit — but nobody decided it, and the tooth's whole job is to make that decision explicit and dated. Law 9: this is red and there is no triage authority to call it pre-existing and move on.

occurrences.found_by: CC, at the CONSTRAIN stage of ticket one-owner-for-the-instance-address. The stage surfaced build_inspector's charter falsifier — 'RED on any of: ... (6) an oracle or outbound import appears in inspector.py' — and the bound was measured rather than assumed. Measured two ways: import_map(inspector.__file__) against the tooth's own tuple returned ['cairn.base.nest'], and running the proof bare reproduced the assertion.
occurrences.verbatim: AssertionError: inspector.py imports outside its allowlist: ['cairn.base.nest'] — the verdict path may never reach the tree (a verdict is always hardware), and the graft's only cairn door is chart's nexus verbs

disposition_owed: A RULING, not an edit, and it is small: either (a) the allowlist gains cairn.base with a dated comment naming ticket the-questions-are-the-sieve (the convention every other entry follows), which requires confirming cairn.base.nest is tree-free transitively the way the tooth's other admissions are pinned; or (b) inspector.py drops the import and reaches the nest another way. Widening an allowlist as a side effect of unrelated work is the failure this record exists to prevent, which is why it is filed rather than fixed in passing.
